newsitem.title: JAPAN: Shokochukin privatisation would not be easy - MITI.
newsitem.headline: Shokochukin privatisation would not be easy - MITI.

text.p: Japan's Trade Minister Shinji Sato said on Tuesday that it would not be easy to privatise the Shokochukin Bank, one of the Japanese government-backed financial institutions whose future is under review.

The ruling Liberal Democratic Party is looking at ways of reforming institutions like Shokochukin, the Central Bank for Commercial and Industrial Cooperatives, as part of attempts to slim down the government.
The LDP's administrative reform panel has said it will present draft proposals for the reforms by late April at the earliest.
Asked about the possibility of privatising the Shokochukin Bank, which is supervised by the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI), Sato told reporters: "It is not an easy proposition."

The government now has a stake of 300 billion yen in the bank and it appears that private banks are not particularly willing to take over the government stake, Sato added. The bank specialises in loans to smaller enterprises.
